diagnostic_interpretation: Probe: 156 independent original streams per core, IRET/RETF widths 2/4/8, CS/outer SS and thirteen descriptor ranges. The recorded fields differ only in 24 tail-case error codes: local P4 reports zero, E12 reports selector 0x24.

Initial generated red: P4 has 48 saved error-code RAM differences at 0x1cfd0, plus 72 successful outer-return differences in unusable data-cache present metadata; E12 has only the 72 cache metadata differences. KVM exposes those invalidated cache attributes differently from the model, which already represents their unusability separately. This boundary test does not define a new unusable-cache metadata policy.

Red2 initializes valid DPL3/RPL3 data caches in both inputs so that outer return does not invalidate them. Complete output State and RAM remain unmasked. E12 passes all 312 comparisons; P4 has exactly the 48 saved error-code differences and no remaining State differences.

The first green attempts expanded immediate-cleanup forms and compiler/optimization combinations, but same-named tests in distinct suites reuse a permanently loaded dynamic-library path. This causes CodeChanged=20 and artifact overwrites; suite-qualified source/library/artifact names fix the test infrastructure. Its IRET event-stop test initially tried to resume the retired instruction token; the runtime correctly moves that work to Delivery.Continuation. The corrected test uses the event resume API and preserves the initial failure record as a test-adapter diagnostic.

native_oracle.method: Fresh VM/vCPU per original stream, two initial SREGS writes, no intermediate host rewrites; KVM_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY fills stage-2 backing. Original and generated code receive identical CPU/RAM inputs. Compare full represented State and all 0x40000 RAM bytes without output masks. Pre-access handler HLT page in both inputs; pre-access wrapped missing-first-page ancestors in both inputs, as in baseline. Data caches remain usable across outer CPL3 return.

profiles.FlagsFirst / SelectorFirstTruncatedIP: Existing range policy: local E core 0x20 reports #GP(selector) for noncanonical descriptor start or tail. RETF truncates compatibility IP before canonicality.
profiles.FlagsFirstTailGPZero / SelectorFirstTail: Local P core 0x40 reports #GP(selector) for noncanonical descriptor start and #GP(0) for only a noncanonical tail. RETF checks original saved compatibility IP.

limitations: Only the pinned local Intel hybrid cores qualify these target choices. Production never infers from its host; unknown core types skip this comparison.

Successful targets in the descriptor matrix retain long CS. Existing complete IRET/RETF matrices separately exercise flags, privilege and compatibility behavior using the qualified new P-core variants.
No initially-clear fault-walk ancestor A policy or partial descriptor-data store is inferred from this matrix. Unusable data-cache metadata is outside these probes; outputs are not masked.
Software suspension tests verify software retention contracts; original CPU executions are uninterrupted.

coverage: Twelve instruction forms: IRET widths 2/4/8; RETF widths 2/4/8 with no immediate, imm16=16 and imm16=65535. Both return CS and outer SS target the thirteen descriptor cases.

Cases cover low/high last descriptors, noncanonical start/tail, absent first translation, high canonical mappings/faults, qword end-to-zero wrap, base-plus-index wrap, accessed writes and either wrapped fragment being read-only.
HighC and LLVMC, host-x64 Clang and NeverC, O0/O2: 2496 full original/generated comparisons per SDK. Nonzero CR2 distinguishes GP preservation from exact first/second fragment PF addresses.

288 suspended comparisons per SDK cover first-frame backing, after accepted CS reads, and after an accessed descriptor write. Both public profile changes refuse before resume effects, preserving original tokens, State, RAM and budget.

Eight IRET comparisons retain NMI unblocking and zero budget across repeated frame backing, refusal, original-profile GP, event-frame backing and event continuation. Retired instruction tokens are not replayed.

Sixty-four full-mode comparisons keep accepted options when a reconstructed outer context supplies the opposite profiles. Unknown direct-owner enum values refuse before NMI, CPU, paging-control or RAM effects.

Selector and return suites share neutral explicit descriptor-range fixture preparation; their original-CPU streams and expectations remain independent. Existing selector and return continuation groups are replayed.
Old enum values keep numeric identity and behavior. Event descriptor policies are unchanged. No additional unobserved truncate-plus-tail profile is introduced.
boundaries: NeverC remains host/source x64; guest widths and modes do not add a 32-bit compiler target.
Full paged-source, legacy-source, shared events/native paging, low instruction boundary and SDK adapter suites are replayed on both SDKs. Previous lower-paging qualification is not recounted.
Event descriptor-tail qualification, remaining mode-aware owners, real/unreal/VM86 composition, software SMM/SGX, unbound asynchronous producers and physical SGX qualification remain open.
Production LLVM remains neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6. No LLVM release, production pin or source gitlink change is included.
